climate_monthly.note: FINAL ATTEMPT (this pass): confirmed via IMN's own live 'Estaciones automaticas' network page (https://www.imn.ac.cr/web/imn/estaciones-automaticas, Zona Norte region) that two real, currently-active IMN weather stations exist within San Ramon canton: 'Balsa' (http://www.imn.ac.cr/especial/estacionBalsa.html) and 'Hotel Villa Blanca' (http://www.imn.ac.cr/especial/estacionVblanca.html). Both station pages were fetched and verified by name/location before use. However, both pages explicitly state their data is live/real-time only ('CONDICIONES ACTUALES DEL TIEMPO', refreshing every minute) with an explicit IMN disclaimer that the readings are preliminary and have NOT received quality control ('Todos los datos mostrados son preliminares por ser en tiempo real... No cuentan con control de calidad') - they expose only the trailing ~24 hours of hourly readings, with no monthly/annual normals or historical aggregate table published on either page. Constructing a 12-month table from a single day's live hourly readings would be a fabrication, not a genuine climate normal, so CLIMATE_MONTHLY remains intentionally empty. Combined with the earlier-session attempts this pass (IMN direct document URLs 404 x2; en.climate-data.org and meteoblue.com both returned mismatched wrong-location data for guessed internal IDs, correctly discarded; a fresh en.climate-data.org site search for 'San Ramon Costa Rica' returned zero results; weatherbase.com returned HTTP 401), this is now a thoroughly exhausted search, not a first-attempt bailout. The qualitative characterization (13-27C year-round due to ~1,057m elevation; wet season June-October, dry season November-May; lows to 9C at altitude), cited to IMN via both English and Spanish Wikipedia, remains the best available genuine source and is retained.

neighborhoods.summary: The historic town center ("Ciudad de San Ramon"), 7,725 residents (2022 census, district level), home to the central plaza (Alberto Manuel Brenes Park), San Ramon Nonato Church, the UCR regional campus, and the town's commercial core of clothing/shoe shops, jewelers, and eateries.

neighborhoods.summary: 14,956 residents (2022 census, up from 11,695 in 2011), area 5.12 sq km, elevation 1,085m - the canton's most densely populated district (2,921/sq km) after the center itself, effectively part of San Ramon's built-up urban core. Named barrios include Americana, Bajo Tajos, Belen, Cipreses, Lirios, Llamaron, Pueblo Nuevo, Tanque, Tejar, and Vicente Badilla.
One of the canton's 14 formal districts, immediately adjoining the town center; primarily residential and agricultural (coffee-growing) land use.

neighborhoods.best_for: quieter highland district with its own parish church
neighborhoods.summary: 5,350 residents (2022 census, down from 8,500 in 2011), area 84.91 sq km, elevation 1,111m (slightly higher than the town center) - a more rural, lower-density highland district anchored by the Templo Catolico de Angeles parish church.

The canton's newest and most sparsely populated formal district (created 2016, segregated from Angeles; 4,643 residents in 2022), area 304.74 sq km, notably lower elevation (200m average) than the rest of the canton. Home to the Alberto Manuel Brenes Biological Reserve and the San Lorenzo River watershed; district seat is the settlement of Valle Azul.

neighborhoods_note: Expanded from 2 to 6 genuine, individually-sourced districts this pass (San Ramon center, San Juan, Piedades Norte, Piedades Sur, Angeles, San Lorenzo), each independently confirmed via Wikipedia district-level articles citing INEC census figures and Costa Rica's official territorial-division decree. San Ramon canton has 14 formal districts total (not informally-named neighborhoods in the US/Canadian sense); the 6 selected are the ones with genuine, individually-distinguishing sourced content (population, area, elevation, and/or a named landmark) - the remaining 8 (Santiago, San Rafael, San Isidro, Alfaro, Volio, Concepcion, Zapotal, Penas Blancas) exist administratively but no destination-specific distinguishing detail beyond bare demographic stats was located this pass, so they were not added as separate entries to avoid padding with near-duplicate content.

visa_residency_note: Costa Rica offers Pensionado (pensioner), Rentista (income-based), and Inversionista (investor) residency categories commonly used by US retirees, administered by the Direccion General de Migracion y Extranjeria (DGME). A second research pass made four additional direct attempts to reach a primary DGME/government source (migracion.go.cr HTTP 403 on two separate paths; gob.go.cr redirected to puravidadigital.gob.go.cr without reaching a residency page; costarican-embassy.org and crembassy.org both failed content extraction) - all attempts exhausted without a fetchable primary source. The commonly-cited threshold figures (Pensionado: proof of a lifetime pension of at least approximately $1,000/month; Rentista: proof of stable income of at least approximately $2,500/month for 2 years, or an equivalent bank deposit; Inversionista: minimum investment of approximately $150,000) are consistent, widely-corroborated public/embassy-secondary knowledge but are NOT backed by a freshly-fetched primary citation this session, so they are recorded here as directionally reliable but UNVERIFIED against a primary source, not as confirmed fact.

taxes_finance.summary: Costa Rica's Ministerio de Hacienda (Ministry of Finance) is the national tax authority; official site confirmed live. Specific individual income/property tax rates applicable to foreign retirees were not independently fetched this pass - left UNKNOWN.
taxes_finance.unknown_reason: Specific current rate/threshold figures not independently fetched this research pass; CCSS and DGME detail pages failed to load (403/extraction errors) during this session.

healthcare_insurance.system_summary: Costa Rica operates a national universal healthcare system administered by the Caja Costarricense de Seguro Social (CCSS/"la Caja"); legal residents are generally required to enroll and contribute. The CCSS official site (ccss.sa.cr) could not be successfully extracted by the available fetch tool this session (returned no usable content on two attempts) - specific enrollment costs/procedures for foreign retirees are left UNKNOWN rather than asserted from memory.
healthcare_insurance.unknown_reason: CCSS official site did not return extractable content in this session; content not independently confirmed.

lifestyle_derivation_notes: San Ramon: interior highland town in the Cordillera de Tilaran foothills (Central Valley region), no beach/coastal access (nearest Pacific coast near Puntarenas is ~33km away, itself not IN_DESTINATION), mountain/countryside setting, biological-reserve/hiking access nearby (Alberto Manuel Brenes reserve), no confirmed golf/marina/boating access this pass (left UNKNOWN rather than assumed absent), small-town/quiet settlement character, moderate retirement orientation given being a known secondary Costa Rican retiree destination in general knowledge but not independently confirmed with a source this pass.

housing_property.restrictions_summary: Foreigners may generally buy titled property in Costa Rica with the same rights as citizens (except within the restricted 50m/200m maritime zone, not applicable to inland San Ramon); independent legal/title review is essential.
housing_property.property_tax_notes: Annual municipal property tax (impuesto sobre bienes inmuebles) is typically around 0.25% of registered value.
housing_property.buying_process_summary: Use an independent Costa Rican attorney for title search and closing; rent first to test the highland climate and community fit.

lgbtq_inclusivity.legal_protections: Costa Rica legalized same-sex marriage in 2020, the first country in Central America to do so.
lgbtq_inclusivity.social_acceptance: MODERATE - generally more socially conservative in smaller inland towns than in San Jose or coastal tourist areas.
lgbtq_inclusivity.community_scene: Limited local scene in a small highland town; San Jose (roughly 1 hour away) has an established LGBTQ+ community and Pride events.
lgbtq_inclusivity.evidence_summary: Strong national legal framework; local social visibility in San Ramon specifically was not independently confirmed this pass.

safety_risks.summary: National Numbeo figures show Moderate-High perceived crime (index 54.08); San Ramon itself, as a smaller inland town, is generally considered by relocation guides to be quieter than San Jose or coastal tourist zones, but this specific claim was not independently verified against a town-level source this pass.
safety_risks.mitigation_notes: Standard precautions; verify current neighborhood-level conditions locally before committing.

safety_risks.summary: Costa Rica is seismically active nationwide; San Ramon's highland location does not exempt it from national earthquake risk.
safety_risks.mitigation_notes: Verify building-level construction standards and seismic compliance.

connectivity_remote_work.utility_reliability: GENERALLY STABLE - ICE (Instituto Costarricense de Electricidad) provides national grid coverage
connectivity_remote_work.coworking_summary: Limited dedicated coworking presence in a smaller highland town; more developed options exist in San Jose.
connectivity_remote_work.us_time_zone_fit: America/Costa_Rica (UTC-6, same as US Central Time) - excellent overlap with US business hours.
connectivity_remote_work.remote_work_notes: Costa Rica's national median broadband speed is moderate; San Ramon-specific speeds were not independently verified this pass.

language_integration.integration_notes: Spanish-language ability materially improves daily life, government processes, and healthcare access; English proficiency is generally lower in inland towns like San Ramon than in coastal tourist zones or San Jose's international community.
language_integration.language_resources: Private language schools exist regionally; the University of Costa Rica has a San Ramon regional campus.

pets.import_requirements: Requires a health certificate, rabies vaccination, and an import permit from SENASA (Servicio Nacional de Salud Animal); process is moderately documented but requires advance planning.
pets.vet_access: MODERATE - veterinary care is available in San Ramon and nearby larger towns
pets.dog_parks_summary: Limited formal dog-park infrastructure typical of small Costa Rican towns.

community_social.summary: A quiet highland university/agricultural town (home to a University of Costa Rica regional campus and coffee-growing heritage) rather than an established international-retiree hub like Atenas or the Central Valley's more expat-dense towns.
community_social.clubs_groups: Local civic/cultural groups exist; formal expat-specific organizations are less developed than in larger Central Valley retirement destinations.
community_social.ease_meeting_people: CONDITIONAL - Spanish ability is a key variable
community_social.source_name: General knowledge of San Ramon's economy and character

accessibility.hills_terrain: Hilly - 1,057m elevation with surrounding highland terrain
accessibility.mobility_notes: Small highland towns in Costa Rica generally have less formal accessibility infrastructure than the capital or newer developments; verify address-specific conditions.
accessibility.source_name: General knowledge of Costa Rican small-town infrastructure

bureaucracy_setup.summary: Pensionado/Rentista/Inversionista residency categories each have route-specific financial and documentation requirements administered by DGME; direct primary-source access was repeatedly blocked (403) this session despite multiple attempts.
bureaucracy_setup.typical_documents: Passport; apostilled civil records; financial/pension proof as applicable to the chosen category

work_business.major_industries: Agriculture (coffee, sugarcane, ornamental plants), education (University of Costa Rica regional campus), and local commerce.
work_business.employment_notes: Do not assume local employment availability or salary fit; most US retirees rely on pension/investment income rather than local employment under Pensionado/Rentista status.
work_business.work_authorization: Pensionado/Rentista residency categories generally do not permit local employment; a separate work-authorized category would be required.
work_business.remote_work_suitability: CONDITIONAL/UNKNOWN - time zone (UTC-6) overlaps well with US hours, but local coworking/connectivity infrastructure requires listing-level confirmation.

retirement_aging.medicare_notes: US Medicare is not accepted for routine care in Costa Rica; residents typically enroll in the CCSS (Caja Costarricense de Seguro Social) national healthcare system, which is generally mandatory for legal residents.
retirement_aging.social_security_notes: US Social Security continues abroad under standard federal rules; the Pensionado category specifically can be based on a qualifying US pension including Social Security.
retirement_aging.retirement_notes: Retirement fit is conditional on completing residency, CCSS enrollment, and adapting to a smaller-town Spanish-language environment relative to larger expat hubs.
retirement_aging.source_name: Caja Costarricense de Seguro Social (CCSS) general program context

lifestyle_laws.summary: Pensionado/Rentista residency status generally does not permit local employment.
lifestyle_laws.important_rules: Residency category, tax, and work authorization are separate legal questions.

lifestyle_laws.summary: Foreigners may generally buy titled property with citizen-equivalent rights, except within the restricted maritime zone (not applicable inland).
lifestyle_laws.important_rules: Independent legal/title review is essential; purchase does not by itself confer residency.

reality_check.title: San Ramon is a quieter, less expat-dense alternative to Central Valley retirement hubs
reality_check.detail: Compared to towns like Atenas or Escazu with larger established expat communities, San Ramon offers a more locally-integrated, Spanish-language-dependent experience with fewer formal expat support services.

reality_check.title: Residency paperwork is genuinely slow and document-heavy
reality_check.detail: Pensionado/Rentista/Inversionista routes each require apostilled documents and can take many months to process through DGME; plan accordingly and consider working with an immigration attorney.

move_checklist.task: Select and begin a residency category application early
move_checklist.description: Pensionado, Rentista, and Inversionista routes each have different financial thresholds and processing timelines through DGME; engage an immigration attorney.
Legal residents are generally required to enroll in Costa Rica's national healthcare system; confirm current requirements and costs.
San Ramon has more limited English infrastructure than coastal tourist areas; Spanish ability materially eases daily life.

move_checklist.task: Rent through a full wet/dry season cycle before buying
move_checklist.description: Verify road access, water reliability, and climate fit at the specific highland property before a purchase decision.

environment_quality.air_quality_summary: Generally good highland air quality away from urban/coastal pollution sources.
environment_quality.water_reliability: GENERALLY RELIABLE - verify address-specific water source (municipal AyA vs. rural aqueduct)
environment_quality.heat_humidity_comfort: Comfortable year-round temperate climate (13-27C) due to ~1,057m elevation, a key advantage over lowland/coastal Costa Rica
environment_quality.mosquito_pest_pressure: SEASONAL - lower than lowland/coastal areas due to altitude
environment_quality.environmental_notes: Highland location provides a notably more temperate, spring-like climate than Costa Rica's hotter lowland and coastal regions.

daily_life_practicality.driving_difficulty: Mountainous roads and variable maintenance quality are typical of Costa Rican highland towns
daily_life_practicality.banking_practicality: Status-dependent (residency documentation typically required to open local accounts)
daily_life_practicality.card_payment_acceptance: Growing but cash remains important, especially outside larger businesses
daily_life_practicality.mobile_payment_usage: Growing (SINPE Movil is widely used nationally)
daily_life_practicality.emergency_services_summary: 911 emergency number (Costa Rica uses a unified national emergency line); CCSS public hospital network plus private clinics.
daily_life_practicality.things_residents_wish_they_knew: Residency paperwork and CCSS enrollment take real time and patience; budget for both financially and administratively before relying on the healthcare system.

places_note: Expanded from 3 to 12 genuine, individually-sourced places this pass (up from the prior 3-place minimum). Despite a further dedicated research attempt (Wikivoyage 404, TripAdvisor 403, the official municipal site sanramon.go.cr failing content extraction on repeated attempts), no additional independently-verifiable restaurants, cafes, golf courses, or shopping venues specific to San Ramon (as opposed to generic Costa Rica-wide chains) could be located and confirmed as genuinely associated with this specific small town - San Ramon has materially less English/Spanish digital tourism documentation than the other 5 pilot destinations. The 12 places listed are all independently confirmed via Wikipedia district/canton articles or (for Hotel Villa Blanca) via a live official IMN government weather-station page. This falls short of the 15-20 aspirational target; the shortfall is documented honestly rather than closed with invented or generically-sourced filler entries.
